fills.researcher_notes: Two independent sources, and they use two DIFFERENT (and complementary, not conflicting) Russian pipe-diameter conventions: proektneftegaz.ru's reconstruction-project scope explicitly states Ду700 (условный диаметр / nominal bore, 700mm) for this line, matching the recorded value exactly. energybase.ru states 720mm, which is Дн (наружный диаметр / actual outer diameter) — for Russian trunk-line steel pipe, a nominal Ду700 line is standardly built from 720mm-OD pipe (the wall thickness accounts for the ~20mm difference); this is the same well-known Дн720/Ду700 pairing seen elsewhere in this batch (e.g. P1456 records Diameter=720 directly, i.e. the Дн convention). Read together these describe the SAME physical pipe, not a discrepancy — staged at high with the convention explained rather than flagged as a spec conflict.

Historically this pipeline is unusual: built 1945-48 to carry SHALE GAS (газосланцевый / горючий сланцевый газ) manufactured at Kohtla-Järve's oil-shale gasification plant to Leningrad (confirmed via vkg.ee company history: '1948...1952 Household gas is pumped to Leningrad and Tallinn', and stena.ee's account of the 1945 decision to build 'the world's first shale-gas plant' at Kohtla-Järve specifically to supply Leningrad with household gas). Multiple independent secondary sources (search results citing the pipeline's history) state that from the mid-1950s/1957 the line was reversed/repurposed to carry Russian NATURAL gas from the Unified Gas Supply System into Estonia instead, once Siberian natural gas became available and the shale-gas plants' output was redirected to chemical feedstock use. I could not find a document naming the SPECIFIC current upstream field/stream (e.g. Vuktyl, Yamal) that feeds this particular line today, nor confirm gas still flows through it at all in either direction given BISI's 'no longer commercially used since 2019' finding (see Status [ref]/status_reviews) — a specific FuelSource value would be a guess. status_reviews.summary: Status=operating remains correct. Commercial cross-border gas trade on this line stopped in 2019 (three years before Estonia's 2022 general ban on Russian gas imports, and for reasons unrelated to it — Estonia's own broader shift away from Russian gas supply contracts). BISI's April 2025 report states the connection 'remains available for technical gas supply to system operators and pipeline stations' — i.e. the physical pipeline is intact, maintained, and technically in-service within the Unified Gas Supply System, even though it is not currently carrying commercial export/import volumes. Per the brief's own rule, a line that has stopped exporting but remains in the Unified System is operating, not idle/mothballed/retired — there is no GEM controlled-vocabulary status for 'technically available, commercially unused' short of 'operating'.
status_reviews.caveat: Note for context (not a status change): commercial use ceased in 2019, predating the 2022 Estonia Russian-gas embargo by three years. If GEM later wants a distinct 'idle/standby' status for pipelines carrying zero commercial flow while remaining technically available, this row would be a candidate — but no such value exists in the current controlled vocabulary, and BISI's own language ('remains available') supports keeping operating.
status_reviews.researcher_notes: Read the full BISI report (independent UK think-tank, not Gazprom/GEM/Russian-state-linked) rather than relying on a snippet. Cross-checked against Elering's (Estonian TSO) own gas network development plan, which shows Estonia's current primary Russia-interconnection point is at Izborsk/Pskov, not Kohtla-Järve — confirming this specific pipeline is a distinct, separate corridor that has not carried Estonia's modern import volumes for some time, consistent with BISI's 2019 commercial-halt date rather than contradicting the operating verdict.

Worth checking against P5589's recorded length/diameter/pressure when that row is researched — if it matches, this is a usable Length/Diameter/Pressure ref for P5589 too.

summary: P2326 re-audited: existence/route/classification all confirmed as a genuine, well-documented 1945-48 Kohtla-Järve-Leningrad trunk gas pipeline (Gazprom Transgaz Saint Petersburg / Gazprom PJSC 100%). All 15 worklist units resolved (13 REFS_ADDED/REVERIFIED with 2-independent-source corroboration on most, 2 UNRESOLVED: FuelSource, SegmentCost). Diameter Ду700/Дн720 and Length 203km-vs-260km apparent conflicts investigated and resolved (unit-convention and outlier-source explanations, not real discrepancies). Location: StartState/Province corrected from bare 'Estonia' to 'Ida-Viru County' (START_MISMATCH fix), filed as both a fill and an attribution validity concern. Status review: confirmed operating — commercial flow halted 2019 (pre-dating the 2022 Estonia embargo) but line remains technically available/in the Unified System per BISI 2025-04. 3 cross-row leads filed for P5589.
